Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - When `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` contains open PR review threads: - Write one Markdown file per open thread under `outputs/review_replies/`. - Write `outputs/review_replies.json` with one entry per open thread, including `inReplyToId`, `threadId`, and a `reply` field that contains the path to the matching `.md` file. - Do **not** put reply bodies inline in the JSON. ## PR Rework — Output Rules Rework posts **only** to the Pull Request. All output must be Markdown. ### Required files 1. `outputs/response.md` - Markdown fix summary for the top-level PR comment. - Use `#`/`##` headings, ` ``` ` code fences, `-` bullets. - Required sections: `## Issues/Notes`, `## Approach`, `## Files Modified`, `## Test Coverage`. 2. `outputs/review_replies.json` - **Mandatory** when the PR has open review threads. - If there are no open threads, write `{ "replies": [] }`. - Format: ```json { "replies": [ { "inReplyToId": 1234567890, "threadId": "", "reply": "outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md" } ] } ``` 3. `outputs/review_replies/*.md` - One Markdown file per open PR review thread. - The file path is referenced from `outputs/review_replies.json` via the `reply` field. - Keep each reply concise and factual; reference the fix location when possible. Rules for review replies: - Read `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` to obtain each open thread's `threadId` and `rootCommentId` (`inReplyToId`). - Create one reply entry and one `.md` file for **every** open review thread — do not skip any unresolved conversation. - `threadId` is required to resolve/close the conversation; `inReplyToId` is required to post the reply in the correct thread. - ⚠️ **Copy `threadId` verbatim, character-for-character, from `pr_discussions_raw.json`.** Its format depends on which SCM the PR lives on (a GitHub GraphQL node ID, a GitLab discussion hash, an ADO thread number, etc.) and is opaque — never invent, prefix, reformat, or pattern-match it against an example. The value above is a placeholder showing *where* the field goes, not what it should look like. - Do **not** put the reply body inline in the JSON; use the `reply` field only as a file path reference. - ⚠️ **Common mistake**: `pr_discussions_raw.json` uses the field names `rootCommentId` and `body`. When writing `review_replies.json`, you MUST rename these to `inReplyToId` and `reply` respectively — do NOT copy the input field names as-is into the output JSON, or the reply will silently post as an untargeted top-level comment instead of a threaded reply. ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. Use dmtools only for additional data (e.g., parent story details, linked tickets not in input/). Use `dmtools` CLI only when data is **not** already in `input/`. ```mermaid flowchart TD NEED["Need external context?"] --> CHECK{"Already in input/?"} CHECK -->|Yes| READ["Read local files — NO API call"] CHECK -->|No| SOURCE{"Source"} SOURCE -->|Jira| J["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY
dmtools jira_search_by_jql JQL"] SOURCE -->|Confluence| C["dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL
dmtools confluence_search QUERY"] SOURCE -->|ADO| A["dmtools ado_get_work_item ID
dmtools ado_search_work_items QUERY"] SOURCE -->|GitHub| G["dmtools github_get_issue REPO NUM
dmtools github_search_code QUERY"] J --> PARSE["Parse JSON → use in response"] C --> PARSE A --> PARSE G --> PARSE subgraph RULES["⚠️ Rules"] R1["Check input/ first — avoid redundant fetches"] R2["Handle errors gracefully — continue with available info"] R3["Cite sources — mention where data came from"] end PARSE --> RULES NOTE["Examples:
dmtools jira_get_ticket PROJ-456 [jira-ticket]
dmtools confluence_search 'parser spec'
dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL"] -.-> NEED ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph USE["Use dmtools skill"] U1["Jira, Figma, Confluence, Teams, etc."] U2["Credentials preconfigured via environment variables"] end subgraph SAFETY["CLI command safety"] S1["One simple executable command at a time"] S2["DMTools rejects shell metacharacters"] end subgraph FORBIDDEN["NEVER USE"] F1["Pipes: |"] F2["Redirection: > < 2>/dev/null"] F3["Chaining: ; && ||"] F4["Substitution: backticks, $(), ${...}"] end subgraph EXAMPLES["Instead"] E1["find ... | head -20"] --> E1a["run: find ..."] E2["cmd1 && cmd2"] --> E2a["run: cmd1"] --> E2b["then: cmd2"] E3["Complex logic"] --> E3a["Write script file, run script as single command"] end subgraph CWD["Working directory discipline (persistent shell!)"] C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"] C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source? You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"] C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"] C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"] C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"] C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>). Run pwd first if unsure; only cd once per direction change"] C7["For one-off commands inside a dependency checkout, prefer git -C dependencies/<repo> <command> over cd dependencies/<repo> then command — the -C form targets that directory without depending on or changing the shell cwd, so there is no cd bookkeeping to get wrong"] C8["Git global flags like --no-pager go BEFORE the subcommand: git --no-pager diff ... is correct, git diff ... --no-pager errors out (git treats the trailing flag as a positional argument)"] end USE --> SAFETY SAFETY --> FORBIDDEN SAFETY --> EXAMPLES SAFETY --> CWD ```

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

# gh-50: feat(machine): stream child command output live to stderr in cli_execute_command (kill the log-file scaffolding)

## Description

## Feature (operator pain observed live, 2026-09-12)

When the AI Teammate machine runs an agent, CI shows **nothing while it works** — the agent's stdout reaches the Actions log only at the end, as one escaped JSON blob (dmtools `cli_execute_command` captures the child's combined output and returns it as a string — that's the JS-bridge contract and it must stay).

The workflow currently papers over this with a `FA_LOG_FILE` + `tail -F | sed` side-channel. That scaffolding should not exist.

## Request: live tee in `cli_execute_command` (and the CliAgent path)

While still capturing the combined output for the return value, **mirror every child output line to dmtools' own stderr live** (line-buffered, as lines arrive — not buffered until exit). Stderr keeps the captured-string contract intact for JS scripts and tool callers; humans (and CI logs) get the live stream for free.

- Applies to the process-execution path used by `cli_execute_command` (dart `Process.start` streaming instead of `runSync`-style capture, or capture+tee).

====================================================================================================
THREAD 22 PRRT_kwDOTw8Iwc6hyr9k -> .github/workflows/ai-teammate-issues.yml
🚨 **BLOCKING: this PR silently reverts the gh-63 credential hardening — red `quality` CI and a fail-open push path**

The rewritten *Configure Git Author + push credentials* step drops every safeguard gh-63 added, and the pinning tests prove it: `test/machine_kit/source_git_credentials_test.dart` fails in **14 places** on the head commit (quality run [103595160838](https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/actions/runs/34709366188/job/103595160838)) — "helper is host-scoped", "purge evidence is a gate, not a printout", "both files call the shared script", "trace dry-run is a real gate", etc.

Concrete regressions in this step:

1. **Fail-open fallback.** When `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` is empty, the step prints a `::warning::` and continues. gh-63 made a leftover App-token extraheader `exit 1` — with the token absent, pushes now silently authenticate as `github-actions[bot]`, the exact failure mode gh-63 was built to prevent.
2. **Helper installed on the generic `credential.helper` key.** This helper answers credential queries for **every** host, not just github.com. gh-63 required the host-scoped `credential.https://github.com.helper` (one of the 14 failing assertions).
3. **Shared script abandoned.** `machine-kit/scripts/install-source-git-credentials.sh` (one audited copy serving both push paths) is replaced by an inline one-liner, so this step and the memory-persist re-assert can drift apart again — the drift the script was created to eliminate.
4. **Gates deleted, not replaced.** The pre-agent trace step (extraheader purge assertion, submodule probe, dry-run credential proof) and the post-agent re-assert are gone with no equivalent.

Nothing in the gh-50 ticket or the PR body justifies touching this machinery. Either restore the gh-63 step/trace gates (call the shared installer), or — if the revert is intentional — delete/update the 14 pinning tests in the same PR and explain the security tradeoff in the PR description. Shipping both the revert and the failing tests is not an option.
====================================================================================================
THREAD 23 PRRT_kwDOTw8Iwc6hyr-s -> .github/workflows/ai-teammate-issues.yml
🚨 **BLOCKING (security): `persist-credentials: false` removed from the checkout — the App token is re-armed with no remaining gate**

Deleting `persist-credentials: false` means `actions/checkout@v4` writes its GitHub App token back into `http.https://github.com/.extraheader` — in the main repo **and in every submodule** (`submodules: true` arms `agents/` too).

Before this PR that was defense-in-depth: the token was never persisted, *and* the trace step fail-closed (`exit 1`) if anything resurrected it, *and* the submodule configs were probed. After this PR all three layers are gone:

- the inline configure step only unsets the extraheader **when `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` is non-empty** (otherwise warning-only, see the thread on line 301);
- nothing purges or even inspects the **submodule** configs anymore, so a push made from inside `agents/` authenticates as `github-actions[bot]`;
- nothing fails the run when the App token survives.

Net effect: a gh-50 streaming PR re-opens the exact "push as github-actions[bot]" hole gh-63 closed (bot-authored commits can't push workflow files and don't trigger workflows). Restore `persist-credentials: false` — it is orthogonal to the log-streaming feature and costs nothing.
====================================================================================================
THREAD 24 PRRT_kwDOTw8Iwc6hysAX -> .github/workflows/ai-teammate-issues.yml
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: trace artifact upload moved back *before* the memory-persist push, and `credential-helper.log` dropped**

The deleted comment documented why this step must run **after** *Persist fa project memory*:

> Must run AFTER the memory-persist push: the artifact is the durable copy of the run … uploaded earlier it would silently miss the last push of the run.

The new ordering reintroduces that gap — the artifact no longer contains anything written to `.dmtools/` by the memory-persist step — and `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` was removed from the upload paths (moot while the helper-log machinery is reverted, but it must come back with the gh-63 restore requested in the other threads).

If the upload stays here by design, update the comment to say why the final push's trace no longer matters; otherwise move the step back below memory-persist and restore the `credential-helper.log` path.

          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"

      - run: dart analyze
      - name: dart test --coverage=coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red suite red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step so the full suite runs ONCE per job.
--
          # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
          # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
          # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact 2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage
        id: coverage
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
          COV=$(grep -o 'end_of_record' coverage/lcov.info | wc -l)

dmtools --version

      - name: Configure Git Author + push credentials
        # gh-63: purge the checkout's persisted App token (github-actions[bot])
        # and make SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN the credential that wins for github.com
        # pushes. All logic lives in the shared installer — one copy serves
        # every push path in the job (this step + the memory-persist
        # re-assert below), so it cannot drift between call sites.
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash machine-kit/scripts/install-source-git-credentials.sh

      - name: Write the issue into the agent input folder
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          # ticket.json carries the tracker-contract fields (key/number/
          # title/body/labels): dmtools hydrates it into params.ticket for
          # every JS action (GOAL.md → Core abstractions → Tracker), so
          # scripts read params.ticket.key exactly like on a Jira machine.
          mkdir -p "input/gh-${NUMBER}"
          gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json number,title,body,url,state,labels \
            -q '{key: ("gh-" + (.number|tostring)), number: .number,
                 title: .title, body: .body, url: .url, state: .state,
                 labels: [.labels[].name]}' \
            > "input/gh-${NUMBER}/ticket.json"
          gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json title,body -q '.title, .body' > input/ticket.md
          echo "input/ticket.md: $(wc -l < input/ticket.md) lines"
          echo "input/gh-${NUMBER}/ticket.json: $(wc -c < input/gh-${NUMBER}/ticket.json) bytes"

      - name: Trace git credential stack (push-time evidence)
        # gh-63 Task 1 — same run that pushes, right before the agent.

391:      - name: Run agent (fa provider via runner env overrides)
      - name: Run agent (fa provider via runner env overrides)
        env:
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          RUNNER: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.runner }}
          # fa provider contract (env preconfig; the runner JSON also pins
          # these via params.envVariables — job env beats it, this step env
          # matches it. Keys: workflow-level separation, same names as
          # machine-kit/teammate-install/dmtools.env).
          AI_AGENT_PROVIDER: fa
          # fa session identity (run-agent.sh -> fa-session.sh): deterministic
          # name fa-<repo>-gh-<n>-<group>-<hash8>, resume-or-create; the cache
          # steps carry it across CI runs.
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.config }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_DISPLAY_KEY: GH-${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONCURRENCY_KEY: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
          KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          # FULL session trace: run-agent.sh passes FA_LOG_FILE to
          # `fa --log-file` (fa >= v0.1.335, flutter_agent_harness#91),
          # which tees every line fa prints — assistant text and tool
          # calls, untruncated — to the file, uploaded as an artifact
          # below. dmtools mirrors child output live to its own stderr
          # (gh-50), so the agent's work already streams into this step's
          # log as it happens; the follower side-channel is gone.
          FA_LOG_FILE="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/fa-trace.log"
          export FA_LOG_FILE
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "${FA_LOG_FILE}")"
          touch "${FA_LOG_FILE}"
          echo "fa full trace: ${FA_LOG_FILE}"
          # Capture the run output for the verdict step below: the final
          # dmtools result is a JSON blob ({"success":…,"results":[{
          # "response":"# PR … verdict: …"}]}) — tee keeps it visible in
          # the step log AND on disk for `Apply the review verdict`.
          RUN_OUTPUT="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/run-output.txt"
          dmtools run "${RUNNER}" \
            --metadata '{"contextId":"gh-${{ github.event.issue.number }}"}' \
            --ciRunUrl "${CI_RUN_URL}" --debug 2>&1 | tee "${RUN_OUTPUT}"
          RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          exit "${RC}"

      - name: Apply the review verdict (review runs only)

if: always() && needs.guard.outputs.kind == 'review'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --remove-label "agent:review" || true
          echo "→ review cycle closed (agent:review removed)"

      - name: Upload the full fa session trace
        # The full untruncated trace file. The step log streams the same
        # output live via dmtools' stderr mirroring (gh-50); the artifact
        # keeps the run readable after log expiry or outside the Actions UI.
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: fa-trace-gh-${{ github.event.issue.number }}-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: |
            .dmtools/fa-trace.log
            .dmtools/run-output.txt
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Persist fa project memory into the repository
        # fa stores project memory under <git-root>/.fah/memory (area:
        # project notes) — committing it makes agent knowledge survive
        # across runs and share between agents. Best-effort: a protected
        # default branch rejects the push, the run stays green and the
        # memory simply lives only in this run.
        if: always()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          git config user.name "dm.ai"
          git config user.email "dm.ai@epam.com"
          if [ -d .fah/memory ] && [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- .fah/memory)" ]; then
            git add .fah/memory
            git commit -m "chore(fa): persist agent project memory [skip ci]"
            git push || echo "::warning::memory push rejected (protected branch?) — kept in run only"
          else
            echo "no new fa memory to persist"
          fi

      - name: Persist fa session to its git branch
        # The save side of the git-based session store (see the restore
        # step): the whole .dmtools/fa-sessions tree of this run lands on
        # fa-sess/gh-<n>, force-pushed — the branch is append-only state,
        # never merged. Runs even on failure: a failed run's session is
        # exactly the context the next rework round needs. Best-effort —
        # a rejected push keeps the run green, the session just does not
        # survive this run.

💡 **SUGGESTION — acknowledged, deferred with rationale**

Agreed the sync `Process.runSync` + `resolveSymbolicLinksSync` in `allowed_base.dart` blocks the isolate on the async `executeCommand` path. Deferring the async/caching rework for now because:

- the reviewer's own assessment applies: the dispatch is short-lived CLI usage — one validation pass per `cli_execute_command` call (two `git rev-parse` spawns + symlink resolution), not a hot loop; and the synchronous JS-bridge path (the primary `cli_execute_command` consumer in agent scripts) is synchronous FFI anyway, where the sync lookups cost nothing extra;
- an async `validateWithinAllowedBase` variant would fork the validation logic into sync/async twins that must stay behaviorally identical (canonicalization rules are pinned by `test/integrations/cli/allowed_base_test.dart`), which is exactly the kind of scope creep this review round is trimming.

Happy to take it as a focused follow-up (async variant + per-base git-root cache) if you want it on this PR instead.

💡 **SUGGESTION — acknowledged; convention fix noted, no code change in this PR**

Fair point: 95 accumulated `.fah/memory/note/*` files bury the 16 files that matter here. Context: this branch is a long-lived dev-run target, so every dev run's *Persist fa project memory* step landed its `chore(fa): … [skip ci]` notes here while the PR stayed open — folding them into the merge history was an artifact of that, not a deliberate choice.

Going forward the workflow's persist step (restored in this round) keeps pushing memory as its own dedicated commit, so future feature branches won't re-fold history the same way; keeping memory out of feature PRs entirely is a harness-workflow convention change we'll take up separately. Rewriting this branch's existing history to split the notes out now would churn every reviewed SHA for zero review value, so we're leaving the already-committed notes as-is.

# PR #57 Rework — CI root cause + open review threads

## Issues/Notes

- **🚨 CI root cause (BLOCKING, threads 22/23):** the gh-50 rewrite of `ai-teammate-issues.yml` had silently reverted the gh-63 push-credential hardening — inline fail-open fallback, generic (not host-scoped) `credential.helper`, shared installer and the fail-closed trace gates deleted, `persist-credentials: false` dropped from checkout. That was the direct cause of the red `quality` runs on `310f49bd`: **14 failing assertions** in `test/machine_kit/source_git_credentials_test.dart` (reproduced locally before fixing).
- **⚠️ Latent second `quality` failure:** with the tests green, CI would have failed the next gate — `crap4dart check --all` reported `test/ai_teammate_review_cycle_test.dart:16: main has 68 lines > max 60` (`method_size`, sources include `test/`). Fixed in the same round.
- **⚠️ `tool/probe_source.dart` (thread 25):** stray live-API debug probe, unreferenced — deleted.
- **Threads 26/27 (suggestions):** acknowledged and answered in-thread, intentionally not code-fixed (see review replies): the sync I/O on the async dispatch path is a short-lived cost the reviewer already deemed non-blocking, and the `.fah/memory` note accumulation is a harness-workflow convention matter — no code change belongs in this PR.
- Top-level review comments also flagged `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` for the agent session (bot-authored events don't trigger workflows) — restored to the PAT-first fallback together with the gh-63 machinery.

## Approach

TDD order per guidelines — reproduce, then fix minimally:

1. **RED:** installed the toolchain (Dart 3.13.3 stable, `make native`, crap4dart 0.9.5) and ran `dart test test/machine_kit/source_git_credentials_test.dart` → 14 failures, matching CI exactly. `dart format`/`dart analyze` already clean on head (the earlier format failure was fixed in a prior round).
2. **GREEN:** restored the gh-63 machinery in `.github/workflows/ai-teammate-issues.yml` from `main`, keeping every gh-50 feature change: `persist-credentials: false`; the *Configure Git Author + push credentials* step back to `bash machine-kit/scripts/install-source-git-credentials.sh`; the *Trace git credential stack* step (extraheader purge assertion, submodule probe, credential dry-run gate) back before *Run agent*; `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}` with its rationale comment; the memory-persist re-assert + post-agent purge gate + helper-invocation evidence. The trace-artifact upload moved back **after** memory-persist with `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` restored to its paths; the gh-50 live-streaming note was merged into the restored comments. Verified the workflow now differs from `main` **only** in the intended gh-50 hunks (follower removal, updated comments).
3. Deleted `tool/probe_source.dart` (no references anywhere).
4. Extracted the two test groups of `test/ai_teammate_review_cycle_test.dart` into top-level functions (all assertions unchanged) to satisfy the 60-line `method_size` gate.
5. Full local loop re-run (AGENTS.md §3): `dart format`, `dart analyze`, `dart test` (with the known `input/`-harness workaround), coverage formatting, `crap4dart check --all`, `crap4dart analyze`.
6. Pushed as `56fc96d` to `ai/gh-50` — CI re-runs automatically.

## Files Modified

- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate-issues.yml` — gh-63 credential hardening restored; gh-50 streaming changes kept; trace upload re-ordered after memory-persist (+ `credential-helper.log` path back).
- `test/ai_teammate_review_cycle_test.dart` — groups extracted to top-level functions (`method_size` gate: main 68 → 9 lines; zero assertion changes).
- `tool/probe_source.dart` — **deleted**.

Commit: `fix(machine): restore gh-63 credential hardening reverted by the gh-50 workflow rewrite` (`56fc96d`).

## Test Coverage

- `test/machine_kit/source_git_credentials_test.dart` — **14 failures → 35/35 pass**; these pin host-scoped helper registration, purge evidence gates, dry-run proof, `persist-credentials: false`, redaction, and the memory-persist re-assert across both YAML files.
- `test/ai_teammate_review_cycle_test.dart` — 9/9 pass (verdict-step wiring + no-`tail -F` pins still hold after the refactor).
- Full suite: **2556 passed, 12 skipped** (integration-tagged, excluded via `dart_test.yaml`) — no regressions; the returned-string contract of `cli_execute_command` is covered by the existing tee/capture suites (`test/integrations/cli/process_output_tee_test.dart`, `cli_tools_test.dart`, `test/agents/cli_execution_mirror_test.dart`), all green.
- Gates: `dart format` clean, `dart analyze` clean, `crap4dart check --all` → **20 passed, 1 warned** (documented Java-parity exemption), 4 skipped; `crap4dart analyze` → Max CRAP 8.00, OK (threshold 8.0).

Per-thread replies: see `outputs/review_replies.json` (6 open threads) with Markdown bodies under `outputs/review_replies/`.

feat(machine): stream child command output live to stderr in cli_execute_command (kill the log-file scaffolding)
## Feature (operator pain observed live, 2026-09-12)

When the AI Teammate machine runs an agent, CI shows **nothing while it works** — the agent's stdout reaches the Actions log only at the end, as one escaped JSON blob (dmtools `cli_execute_command` captures the child's combined output and returns it as a string — that's the JS-bridge contract and it must stay).

The workflow currently papers over this with a `FA_LOG_FILE` + `tail -F | sed` side-channel. That scaffolding should not exist.

## Request: live tee in `cli_execute_command` (and the CliAgent path)

While still capturing the combined output for the return value, **mirror every child output line to dmtools' own stderr live** (line-buffered, as lines arrive — not buffered until exit). Stderr keeps the captured-string contract intact for JS scripts and tool callers; humans (and CI logs) get the live stream for free.

- Applies to the process-execution path used by `cli_execute_command` (dart `Process.start` streaming instead of `runSync`-style capture, or capture+tee).
- No flags, no env toggles — always-on mirroring to stderr. The JS-visible return value is unchanged (same combined string).
- This matches how copilot's CLI behaves in GitHub Actions: you watch the agent work in the step log.

## Acceptance

1. A job that runs `dmtools run <config>` shows the inner agent's output lines appearing in the step log as they are produced.
2. The tool's returned string is byte-identical to today's combined capture (existing tests still pass).
3. `crap4dart` gates stay green (CRAP < 8 — extract a small tee helper; this will touch the process runner used by the tool bridge).

## Delivery

Open a PR to `main` with `Closes #<this issue number>` in the body.

arguments.content:
### What changed
Live tee for `cli_execute_command` (and both CliAgent paths): child stdout/stderr are streamed via `Process.start` and every line is mirrored, line-buffered, to dmtools' own stderr **while** the combined capture string is still returned — the JS-visible contract is byte-identical, CI logs now show the agent working live. The `FA_LOG_FILE` + `tail -F | sed` follower side-channel is removed from `ai-teammate-issues.yml`; merged latest `main` (0.1.8, session-persist fix) with zero drift from the gh-63 credential machinery.

### Key decisions
- Extracted `process_output_tee.dart` (`runCaptured`/`captureAndMirror`): one chunked UTF-8 decoder shared by capture + line-mirror, concurrent stdout/stderr drains (no pipe deadlock), lenient decode + error-path flush, best-effort mirror (a throwing sink can't break capture)
- Always-on mirroring — no flags/env toggles, per ticket; sync JS-bridge path unchanged (FFI host calls are sync, documented deviation)
- `CliToolExecutor.executeCommand` gained a named `mirror:` param (public API was positional-positional before; break called out in CHANGELOG); `workingDirectory` now validated through shared `allowed_base.dart`
